questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why sharks are dangerous to swimmers
How to watch The Great Migration in Kenya
How climate change affects migrating animals, and how they can help fight it
Why sea turtles are disappearing
questions.why: They discuss how climate change affects animal migration and how migrating animals help against climate change.

questions.q: What decides where wildebeest travel during The Great Migration?
options: The movement of lions
The rain
The number of tourists
The length of the day
questions.why: Neil says they travel around the Serengeti and Maasai Mara every year 'depending on the rain'.

questions.q: According to researcher Trisha Atwood, why do animals migrate?
options: Only to escape from hunters
Only because the weather becomes too cold
To find new places to sleep
For food, for mating or to give birth
questions.why: She says some migrate for food resources, mating or giving birth.

questions.q: What example does Trisha give of a long shark migration?
options: Great white sharks swimming from Perth, Australia, to South Africa
Tiger sharks swimming from the coast of Kenya all the way to Tanzania
Sharks travelling from Utah to the Pacific
Sharks crossing from Europe to America
questions.why: She mentions great whites travelling from the coast off Perth all the way to South Africa.

questions.q: What is changing the way sharks migrate?
options: Changes in ocean temperature caused by climate change
Fishing boats
A lack of sea turtles and other creatures for them to eat
Pollution from plastic
questions.why: Neil says climate change is changing ocean temperatures, which changes the way sharks migrate.

questions.q: How do sharks help fight climate change?
options: They eat seagrass that releases carbon
They carry carbon down with them to the bottom of the ocean when they dive
They scare away animals that eat seagrass, which absorbs carbon
They keep the ocean cooler
questions.why: Sharks scare away creatures like sea turtles that eat seagrass, so more seagrass absorbs carbon.

options: Protecting all migrating animals would be enough to stop climate change completely
Managing 10 groups of animals could remove about six gigatonnes a year
Sharks alone remove ten gigatonnes of carbon a year
Wildebeest produce more carbon than they remove
questions.why: She says managing about 10 groups of animals could sequester about six gigatonnes of carbon per year.

questions.q: Why does host Sophie Eastaugh mention the figure of 10 gigatonnes?
options: To show that Trisha's figure is wrong
To say how much carbon sharks produce
To explain exactly how much carbon the seagrass on the ocean floor stores
To help listeners understand how big six gigatonnes is
questions.why: She says 'for perspective' that experts think we need to remove 10 gigatonnes a year.
